name: Account acquisition, credibility building, and reputation manipulation lifecycle
caveats: Geography, nationality, language, camera use, and preference for text communication require lawful, evidence-based review rather than discrimination.
Identity documents, financial details, IP addresses, account credentials, and raw selectors are excluded from publication and retention.
Foreign contractors, customers, local companies, schools, universities, jurisdictions, networks, and service providers require direct evidence before treatment as knowing participants.

Many individual elements appear elsewhere, but the 2022 source supplies an early, coherent account-lifecycle model linking account acquisition, credibility building, bidding, verification evasion, and post-placement expansion.
DPRK attribution requires multiple independently corroborated signals and human review.
These are risk indicators from 2022; current validity and deterministic use require separate evidence.
This is a historical, source-qualified program-level finding; current census and person, organization, jurisdiction, platform-user or technology-user status require current sources.

infrastructure.statement: The advisory describes proxy accounts used to bid, work, and receive payment; account owners selling or lending account access; multiple identities shared within a team; one dedicated device per account in some cases; fabricated education, employment, portfolio, client, statement-of-work, invoice, and communication records; self-dealing between fraudulent client and developer accounts to build ratings; reused document templates; clusters of accounts receiving ratings from one client; extensive bidding with low acceptance; and recruitment of additional workers after one worker is hired.
infrastructure.evidence_class: official intelligence, sanctions, law-enforcement, and compliance synthesis
infrastructure.historical_boundary: These are risk indicators from 2022, not a deterministic signature and not necessarily current in unchanged form.
